newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS FEELS PLAN FLOPPED

Realising its plans to form the next government have gone awry, the Congress planned to open talks with the ruling United Front. The party leadership suffered a setback when the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC), a constituent of the ruling coalition, urged it to reconsider its decision to withdraw support. The Left parties also conveyed their reluctance to back a Congress-led coalition. Congress officials admitted the TMC's move was a dampener because the TMC was a key player in their scheme of things.
The Pioneer
UNITED FRONT POLL CARD UNNERVES CONGRESS

In the war of nerves that marked the countdown to the April 11 confidence vote, the ruling United Front (UF) was trying to call the Congress's bluff by displaying a preparedness to face elections. The prime minister and his men were being supported by loyalists of former prime minister Rao and Maharashtra leader Sharad Pawar's camp. UF sources said claims about mid-term polls were to keep the going tough for the Congress. They admitted that the party, too, could not afford to face polls. The Front hoped to maintain the pressure until the Congress cracked up. Already the scramble for brokering peace between the two secular groupings within the Congress is on.
The Times Of India
FATE OF BUDGET RESTS ON GOVERNMENT'S SURVIVAL

The finance minister's dream budget was the card the ruling United Front decided to play against the Congress. With both business and industry pressing all political parties to ensure passing of the budget, the Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party are in a fix. The lower house of parliament will have a day's special sitting on April 11 to enable the government to seek a vote of confidence. The finance bill could only be passed if the government survives on April 11. At best, a second vote-on-account could be voted on before that.
The Economic Times
LET FINANCE BILL PASS: SPEAKER

The move to secure the passage of the budget appeared to be gathering momentum. The speaker of the lower house, who was approached by the finance and parliamentary affairs ministers seeking his intervention, said failure to pass the budget would lead to a constitutional crisis. He was also confident of political parties acting in a responsible manner to save the situation. The speaker's stand was seen as a concrete sign, amid mounting concern in the Finance Ministry as well as business and industry circles, over the new tax proposals. Political leaders were under pressure also from industry to clear the uncertainty.
RELIANCE, STOCK HOLDING CORP BAG STOCK LENDING LICENCES

Reliance Capital and Stock Holding Corporation of India bagged the first licences to act as intermediaries under the stock lending scheme. The bourse regulator, SEBI, approved the proposals under its recently notified scheme. These were the only two proposals to be submitted so far. The Reliance group has one of the largest treasury operations in the country with large investments in equity instruments and its entry into stock lending assumes significance. Reliance Capital is the financial services arm of the Reliance group. The stock lending scheme notified by SEBI stipulated a net worth of 500 million rupees for intermediaries.
HIGHER RATE OF RETURN FOR HYDEL PROJECTS LIKELY

The new hydel policy being formulated might provide for a higher rate of return for hydel power projects in view of the heavy geo-hydrological risks involved. The government might also allow higher returns on equity for projects supplying power during peak hours. The Power Ministry had recently approached the Finance Ministry for higher budgetary allocations to support the hydel sector. In view of the relatively poor response from the private sector, a committee had suggested a mix of public and private sector projects. The Finance Minister recently stated that the role of public investments would be enhanced.
AVIATION POLICY VETOES INTERNATIONAL CARRIERS

The government will ask private domestic carrier Jet Airways to shed the equity held by Kuwait Airways and Gulf Airways. This followed the new investment norms to keep out foreign carriers from airline joint ventures. Equity from foreign airlines, directly or indirectly, in the domestic aviation sector was not recommended in the new norms. But foreign airport authorities, which do not have any stake by foreign airlines, would be allowed 40 percent stake in domestic airlines, as part of the policy to allow foreign investment in the domestic aviation sector. However, non-resident Indians were allowed 100 percent stake in domestic airlines.
JAPANESE FIRMS MAY SNAP TIES WITH HINDUJAS

Sumitomo and NHI of Japan, the engineering procurement contractor (EPC) of the 1,040-megawatt Hinduja power project, threatened to pull out of the project. The EPC companies, demanding a revision in contract rates to take into consideration factors like inflation and rising market rates, stopped work. The power developer, Hinduja National Power Company, was unable to take any decision as the government was unwilling to consider tariff revisions at this stage. Revision in contract rates would increase the capital cost of the project, thereby making it necessary to revise tariff.
Financial Express
DCM DAEWOO REVAMPS BOARD

In a major restructuring in DCM Daewoo Motors, Daewoo appointed seven full time directors and an executive chairman on a freshly constituted 11 member board. The move followed Daewoo's acquisition of 91.63 percent equity stake in the company. Financial institutions, the DCM group and Toyota Corporation would have one nominee each on the board. DCM Daewoo would be renamed Daewoo Motors (India). The government has cleared the change in name.
ONGC TO RAISE $157 MLN VIA DEBT

The state-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) reworked its financial plans. It decided to raise $157 million by way of debt from various financial institutions and banks, in a bid to part finance its ongoing projects for 1997/98 (April-March). ONGC also postponed its international offering until the end of next year. Work on its public offering would only start after the implementation of the recommendations of Price Waterhouse and McKinsey, appointed to carry out ONGC's financial and corporate restructuring respectively, an official said.
STATE OWNED BANKS SET TO BOUNCE BACK

State-owned banks were set to bounce back into profit, thanks to a 400 basis points cut in cash reserve ratio and a steep decline in the yield to maturity figure for valuation of government securities for 1996/97 (April-March). These banks recorded a 3.29 billion rupee aggregate net loss in 1995/96. The combined net profit of 27 state-owned banks was likely to cross the 20 billion mark, industry analysts said. State Bank would lead the pack with a profit of around 13 billion rupees.
Business Standard
ALTERNATE PLAN READY FOR TATA AVIATION VENTURE

The Tata Group decided to replace Singapore Airlines with other investors who were likely to find favour with the Civil Aviation Ministry. The Tatas had already prepared an alternative plan and the attendant agreements would be signed once the aviation policy was officially communicated to the Tatas. The cabinet approval of the Civil Aviation Ministry's stand that foreign airlines would not be allowed to invest in private domestic airlines had jeopardised the Tata's plan to rope in Singapore Airlines for its 24 billion rupee project.
TRUCKERS CONTINUE STIR

Truck operators decided to continue their countrywide indefinite strike that crippled movement of essential commodities. The Union government asked all states to take contingent measures to tackle the situation. The Finance Ministry might request the parliamentary standing committee on finance to hear the plea of the striking truckers against the proposed service tax on transportation of goods by road.
OMAN OIL LIKELY ON DEFERRED PAYMENT

The government was negotiating a deal with Oman to purchase petroleum products worth 100 billion rupees on a deferred payment basis. The deal, if struck, would abate the pressure on the government to raise petroleum product prices. The prime minister said preliminary negotiations with Oman were fruitful and enough ground work had been done to pull off the deal. The deal would help to put off the petroleum price increase. A cabinet minister confirmed that Oman was keen on the deal, but the final agreement was yet to be reached.
GLOBAL GIANT EYES COAL SECTOR

Global coal mining giant RTZ-CRA was keen on coal blocks with a total capacity of eight million tonnes. The RTZ-CRA move followed a recent decision to permit foreign equity participation in domestic coal companies. The Anglo-Australian group held feasibility studies jointly with state-owned majors Steel Authority and National Thermal Power Corp in the Jharia coalfields in Bihar. However, the company did not find Jharia attractive, sources said. RTZ-CRA was keen to develop coal mines in the Mahanadi coalfield area in Orissa and western coalfields in Maharashtra.
FOREIGN INVESTORS REMAIN NET BUYERS ON BOMBAY BOURSE

Despite weakening markets, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) moved against the market trend and remained net buyers on the Bombay bourse (BSE) after the political crisis exploded. Statistics released by the BSE revealed FIIs remained net buyers, making gross purchases worth 620 million rupees and sales of 70 million rupees, resulting in a net inflow of 550 million rupees on March 31. On April 1, FIIs made gross purchases of 200 million rupees and sales of 70 million rupees, a 130 million rupee net inflow.
The Observer
HITACHI FORMS 100 PCT INDIAN SUBSIDIARY

Hitachi Asia set up a 100 percent owned subsidiary company in India to oversee both Hitachi's existing and future liaison, marketing, sales, trading and investment concerns. Hitachi India would replace the company's existing liaison office and also be the holding company for Hitachi India Trading. Since 1948, Hitachi has been providing equipment and expertise in a wide range of industrial and infrastructure areas in India including power generation, transport, petrochemicals and steel manufacturing.
